excluded_candidates.review_note: The AI catalog accepts Plasma AI's October 19, 2026 claim as full and marks the problem solved. The pinned repository proves Erdos173.erdos_173 with the same arbitrary-coloring and triangle quantifiers as our selected target. I inspected Solution.lean, its definitions, README and comparator configuration, and read the project's replay and statement-fidelity records. Those records report successful compilation, statement comparison and kernel replay with only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. I did not independently rebuild or replay it. The project reports no external referee examination. Bloom's OPEN label is therefore insufficient for eligibility. A stronger one-color-class historical formulation remaining open does not preserve eligibility of this selected theorem.

targets.production_type_pretty: ∀ (n : ℕ) (G : SimpleGraph (Fin n)), Erdos151.cliqueTransversalNumber G ≤ n - Erdos151.H n
targets.review_note: Erdős–Gallai–Tuza bounds and the clique-coloring estimate of Joret–Micek–Reed–Smid give weaker general bounds. The latter yields a transversal bound of the form \(n-c\sqrt{n\log n}\), by taking the complement of a largest color class; this deduction does not recover the exact \(H(n)\). Tuza covers chordal graphs. Veljjanoski's September 2026 submission covers at most 39 vertices and remains a partial claim in the AI catalog.
targets.scope_note: No full solution found; solved graph classes and a finite-order claim.

targets.production_type_pretty: ∀ (k : ℕ), 3 ≤ k → ∃ c > 0, {n | ↑n ^ c < ↑(Erdos322.representationCount k n)}.Infinite
targets.review_note: Mahler's 1936 construction gives polynomially many representations for cubes, including a bound of order \(n^{1/12}\) on twelfth powers. Bloom's exposition derives the construction and explains the unresolved higher-power cases. The selected theorem quantifies over every \(k\ge3\); a solution at \(k=3\) does not resolve it. This is a concrete reason to avoid saying that the candidates have no solved cases.
targets.scope_note: No full solution found; the cubic case is already solved.

targets.production_type_pretty: ∀ n ≥ 1, ∃ k ≥ 1, ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, (n + i) ∣ ∏ i ∈ Finset.range k, (n + k + i)
targets.review_note: Ulas (2013), with Schinzel's appendix, gives a digit-sum criterion, infinitely many witnesses at particular small starting values, and computational witnesses for further values. The paper explicitly does not solve the all-starting-values problem. Its starting-point convention is shifted by one relative to ours. More recent forum computations extend finite ranges, which cannot establish the universal quantifier.
targets.scope_note: No full solution found; particular starting values are settled.

targets.review_note: Luca (2002) proves finiteness for polynomial-factorial equations assuming abc, which implies the selected conclusion under that conjecture. Bui–Pratt–Zaharescu give unconditional power savings in counting solutions, not the required eventual absence for every bounded span. The 2026 Turturean claim also assumes abc. None removes the hypothesis from our theorem.
targets.scope_note: No unconditional full solution found; abc gives a conditional answer.

targets.production_type_pretty: ∀ (f : ℕ+ → ℕ+), Erdos422.IsHofstadterQ f → {n | ∀ (x : ℕ+), f x ≠ n}.Infinite
targets.review_note: Cloitre's July 2026 revision proves totality and asymptotics for the Mantovanelli perturbation, which adds \((-1)^n\) to the recurrence. Related 2026 papers also study perturbed or changed initial conditions. They do not settle the original Q recurrence's omitted-value question. The selected theorem is an implication for a sequence satisfying its predicate; it should not be advertised as separately proving existence or totality of the original recurrence.
targets.scope_note: No full solution found; recent solved recurrences are different.

targets.review_note: Syn's July 2026 research brief explicitly claims no solution. It reports a million steps from seed 7 and arbitrary finite survival with the seed depending on the requested length. The quantifiers differ: a seed for every finite length does not establish a single finite seed surviving forever. Its Lean development also leaves its analytic input explicit. No matching full claim appeared in the checked records or searches.
targets.scope_note: No full solution found; long finite trajectories do not prove infinitude.

targets.review_note: The October 2026 Plasma AI claim gives an exponential bound only when each color class lies in a single sum-free Bohr arc; it is cataloged as partial and unreviewed. Hegde–Lott–Petridis–Ponagandla's August 2026 bound specializes at the Schur parameter to \(3^r r!\), which is not a fixed exponential. Recent lower bounds and fixed-color computations likewise do not settle the target. Bounds for multicolor Ramsey numbers in regimes of growing clique size cannot be substituted for a fixed triangle or Schur problem.

The 1989 Burr–Erdős–Faudree–Schelp theorem evaluates certain clique-plus-extra-vertex Ramsey numbers; it does not compare them with every graph of equal size. Sudakov's general bound in terms of the square root of the edge count also does not identify the exact maximizer. The AI catalog rejects the small-counterexample submission as a resolution of the amended eventual statement, not as invalidating the counterexamples themselves.
